row.team_price_text: Usage-priced: reserved instances from $0.076/hour (4 vCPU, 3-year contract); no per-user plans
row.evidence: OpenShift's identity provider documentation lists htpasswd, Keystone, LDAP, basic auth, request header, GitHub, GitLab, Google and OpenID Connect providers; users are created on first login (mappingMethod 'claim') and no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row, named Red Hat OpenShift. Priced by infrastructure (vCPU-hours or cores), not per user: the pricing page quotes reserved instances from $0.076/hour on a 4 vCPU, 3-year contract, so plan and per-user fields are null. Cluster sign-in uses OAuth identity providers configured as custom resources (OIDC, LDAP, GitHub, GitLab, Google, htpasswd and others; no SAML provider). With the default mappingMethod 'claim' a User and Identity are created on first login (JIT); 'lookup' requires users to be provisioned manually or by an external process. Groups can be synced from LDAP. Admins can manage User and Group objects through the Kubernetes-style user.openshift.io/v1 API, but there is no SCIM endpoint and no IdP catalogue app was found. 'None' is by absence (rule 2: JIT-only is none).

plans.name: Red Hat OpenShift cloud services (ROSA, Azure Red Hat OpenShift, Dedicated, IBM Cloud)
plans.price_text: From $0.076/hour per reserved instance (4 vCPU, 3-year contract); billed by the cloud provider or Red Hat
plans.notes: Infrastructure-priced; self-managed subscriptions are not priced on the page.

scim.notes: The supported identity provider list (htpasswd, Keystone, LDAP, basic auth, request header, GitHub, GitLab, Google, OIDC) has no SCIM; provisioning is JIT on login or manual/external via the User API. 'false' is by absence (rule 5).

auth.notes: OAuth access tokens from the cluster OAuth server; authorization via RBAC.

capabilities.notes: Role assignment is done with Kubernetes RBAC objects, not researched here.

user_api.notes: Kubernetes-style API on each cluster's API server (user.openshift.io/v1 Users, Groups, Identities).

okta.notes: No OIN app found (okta.com/integrations/red-hat-openshift/, /redhat-openshift/, /openshift-container-platform/ and /openshift/ all 404); OpenShift connects to Okta or any IdP as a generic OIDC provider.

entra.notes: No Microsoft Learn gallery tutorial found (red-hat-openshift-tutorial, openshift-tutorial 404).

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP group sync (oc adm groups sync) from an LDAP directory
